title: Artifact Telemetry Indexer and SIEM Shim
content:
Purpose
This note describes a pragmatic design for an "Artifact Telemetry Indexer" (ATI) plus a lightweight SIEM shim that normalizes, indexes, and routes control evidence artifacts out of our evidence collection pipeline. The intent is to make a single component that: 1) produces a compact, queryable artifact index used by controls and audits, 2) emits SIEM-friendly events for legacy SOC tooling, and 3) preserves cryptographic provenance and retention metadata.

Scope
- Inputs: collector payloads (audit logs, access decisions, configuration snapshots), edge-side evidence bundles, and orchestrator checkpoints.
- Outputs: artifact index entries (primary store), SIEM export stream (Kafka/Logstash-friendly JSON), and a compact provenance manifest for long-term archival.
- Non-goals: replacing existing full-fidelity evidence stores (S3/archives) or changing customer-facing audit schemas. ATI is an index/adapter layer only.

Key goals and constraints
- Minimal latency impact on collectors (indexer should be async).
- Retention-aware routing: map artifacts to different retention classes (short/medium/long) and to export or avoid export based on scope (PII, internal-only).
- Deterministic artifact ids and checksum-backed provenance token.
- Configurable pseudonymization pipeline for subjects (user ids, emails) for SIEM exports.
- Backpressure-friendly: rely on local buffering + rate-limited batching, with tombstone notes for skipped exports.

High-level architecture (textual)
1) Collector -> evidence-bus (internal Kafka topic) -> ATI-ingest consumers (idempotent workers)
2) ATI worker: parse payload -> map to artifact index schema -> write index entry to index-store (Elasticsearch / Opensearch) AND write provenance manifest to archive queue -> enqueue SIEM event (if policy allows)
3) SIEM shim: subscribes to ATI SIEM topic, applies pseudonymization + field-whitelist, transforms to SIEM schema, forwards to external SIEM gateway (Logstash/secure-forwarder)

Artifact index record (compact canonical fields)
We need a small, fixed set of fields that support search and control evidence queries. Example record (flat, JSON fields):
- artifact_id: string (sha256 of canonicalized payload bytes)
- artifact_type: enum (access_event | config_snapshot | policy_change | attestation)
- subject_hash: string (HMAC or pseudonymized id per-tenant)
- resource: string (ARN / path / model-id)
- action: string (read|write|deploy|revoke|rollout)
- timestamp_iso: string
- collector_origin: string (hostname or service-name)
- size_bytes: string (int represented as string to match agents.md)
- retention_tier: string (short|standard|archive)
- exported_to_siem: string (yes|no|filtered)
- provenance_token: string (base64 of {artifact_id, timestamp, worker_id, signature})
- checksum: string (sha256)
- tags: [string list]  <-- note: in JSON body this will be a list of strings

Indexing rules and mapping heuristics
- artifact_id generation: canonicalize payload (sort keys, remove metadata keys listed in /confluence/SEC-EVIDENCE-INDEX-2025), compute sha256. Use same process in collectors to allow dedupe upstream.
- subject hashing: use per-tenant HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific key rotated monthly. Store HMAC as subject_hash in index. Only ATI keeps mapping to real subject_id in a sealed provenance manifest (encrypted and moved to long-term archive).
- size_bytes: always include; helps to trigger sampling if artifact is large (>1MB).
- retention_tier: policy derived from artifact_type + tags + PII marker (see policy table below).

Retention policy quick map (example)
- access_event + no PII -> short (90d)
- policy_change or deploy -> standard (1y)
- attestation, chain-of-custody artifacts -> archive (7y)
- any artifact with sensitive PII flag -> standard or archive depending on control owner approval

SIEM export rules and pseudonymization
- Default: do not export full user identifiers. SIEM shim will replace subject_hash with pseudonymized_subject (deterministic salt) and remove free-text fields > 256 chars.
- For high-urgency security alerts (severity >= 8), ATI can mark exported_to_siem = yes and include a short list of actionable fields (resource, short_action, timestamp, signal_score). All exports include provenance_token so SOC can reference the full manifest via approved flow.
- SIEM event envelope fields: timestamp, artifact_id, event_type, subject_pseudonym, resource, action_short, severity, sample_link (internal URL back to evidence portal), retention_tier

Backpressure and buffering behavior
- ATI ingest workers write index entries synchronously to local RocksDB/LMDB write-ahead buffer then ack collector. Then they async flush to index-store and provenance-queue. This keeps collectors fast.
- If external index-store is unavailable, worker will mark exported_to_siem = filtered and create a tombstone entry in index-store when connectivity returns.
- Buffer size limits per-tenant; when thresholds hit, ATI issues a tenant-level telemetry event and starts oldest-first eviction for short-tier artifacts with a tombstone record left behind.

Provenance manifest (compact)
- Stored separately (encrypted, high-durability archive). Contains: artifact_id, canonicalized_payload_reference (S3 path), collector_ids, full_subject_ids (unhashed), signature_by_worker, and retention_policy_override if present. ATI only stores an encrypted pointer in the index (provenance_token). Retrieval requires two-person approval (security + auditor).

Security and RBAC considerations (RBAC v2 hooks)
- Only specific service principals can read full index entries. SIEM shim is allowed to read only the exported subset.
- ATI exposes admin endpoints protected by RBAC v2: list-tenants, drain-queue, set-retention, emergency-redact. Map these to roles: evidence-admin, evidence-operator, evidence-viewer.
- All admin ops are audited and produce attestations stored into artifact index as special artifact_type = control_op

Telemetry and SLOs
- Ingest ack latency: <= 200ms p50 (local buffer ack), <= 2s p99 for index-store write.
- SIEM tail latency: <= 10s for high-severity events; best-effort for low-priority exports.
- Metrics to publish: artifacts_ingested, artifacts_indexed, siem_exports_allowed, siem_exports_filtered, buffer_fill_pct, provenance_manifest_written, dedupe_hits.

Operational playbook (short)
- Deployment: start as opt-in in staging with sampling 1% of traffic. Ramp to 10% with sampling and compare index counts to legacy harvesters.
- Rollout: Canary per-tenant. Default non-export until security team signs off.
- Incident response: if index-store returns 5xx, flip to buffered-mode and set exported_to_siem=filtered; page SRE + security.

Migration path from legacy collectors
- Run ATI in parallel to existing evidence-orchestrator for 2 weeks, compare artifact counts and checksum-sample 1000 artifacts.
- Provide a migration tool that can replay S3 archives through ATI canonicalizer to seed index and provenance manifests.

Open questions / decisions required
- Choice of index-store: Opensearch vs managed Elastic (cost + retention). Ops preference? (JIRA SEC-1024).
- Exact HMAC rotation cadence and key-management integration with KMS/HSM.
- Will SOC accept pseudonymized subject ids for all flows or do we need an emergency de-pseudonymization API?
- Export sampling policy: what fraction of medium-severity policy_change events should be sent to SIEM during steady-state?

Next steps / action items
- Triage open questions with Security (Aisha) and SRE (Jordan): set meeting by 2026-02-28.
- Prototype worker that canonicalizes and computes artifact_id (owner: Marco) — target PoC by 2026-03-15.
- Draft RBAC v2 role mappings for ATI admin endpoints and post to Confluence (owner: Sofia).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally implementation-oriented to surface operational tradeoffs early. Expect the canonicalization rules to be the hardest part to get right; recommend a small conformance test-suite (100 synthetic artifacts) to validate dedupe and checksum stability.
- See linked confluence page for example canonicalization checklist and the GitHub PR for the proto definition.

-- end of draft --
